title: Knowledge graph
content: A knowledge graph is a database of entities, such as people, organizations, products, and places, together with the relationships between them.

meta.why: Google draws on its Knowledge Graph to show facts about an entity in search results, which is where inconsistent public information about your company can surface.
meta.example: A search for a company name shows a panel with the company's founder, headquarters, and official website.
meta.check: Search for your company name, read the knowledge panel if one appears, and compare its facts with your site and your official profiles.
meta.limitation: Google decides which entities appear in its Knowledge Graph, and markup or consistent naming does not guarantee an entry.
